title: Token cost calculator
description: Set tokens per request and traffic, then compare a month of on-demand, batch and Provisioned Throughput, with and without prompt caching.
intro: Most foundation models are priced per token, with separate rates for the tokens you send and the tokens the model writes. Pick a Cairnway preset, then move one slider at a time. Try doubling the output tokens, then doubling the input tokens: which costs more? Then turn the cached prefix down to 0 for the chat preset.
takeaways: On-demand pricing charges per token, with separate input and output rates; output tokens usually cost more. Longer answers also take longer to write.
Batch inference processes many requests together, not in real time. AWS lists select models at a 50% lower price than on-demand: the answer for big jobs that can wait.
Provisioned Throughput is a fixed hourly price per model unit, billed whether or not you use it. It pays off for steady, high traffic and is required to use a custom model on Amazon Bedrock.
Prompt caching reuses a long, repeated start of the prompt to cut input cost and latency. Only supported models offer it, and writing to the cache can cost more, so the savings come from reuse.
Cut cost by sending fewer tokens (shorter prompts, only the relevant context), capping the response length and choosing a smaller model when it is good enough.
